$comment: What you would actually need to build one. NOT a recipe: recipes are the game's two-input grammar and say how a thing is derived. A needs list is the unbounded, honest answer to 'what goes into one', and exists to drive authoring — the corpus checks itself against it and the gaps fall out. Entries may use a|b alternation where two words mean the same thing. See tools/needs.mjs. Where a component name is ambiguous or is a tag rather than an element (`body` means a car body and a human body; `medicine` is a family, not a thing), the list names what the corpus actually calls it.

house.note: A builder's list, in the order the site works: ground, structure, envelope, services, finish.

steam_engine.note: In the order the steam travels: raise it, admit it, use it, condense it, and turn the push into a turn.

generator.note: Faraday's law made into hardware: a magnetic field, a conductor, and relative motion between them.

transformer.note: Two coils sharing one iron path, and the ratio between their turns is the whole device.

battery.note: Two different metals and something that will carry ions between them.

telephone.note: Sound to current and back again, with a way to say who you are calling.

telegraph.note: The first electric network, and it needed almost nothing: a key, a wire, and a code.

loom.note: Every loom does the same four things in the same order, and everything else is speed.

sewing_machine.note: The lockstitch needs two threads that never pass through each other, which is why the needle has its eye at the point.

plough.note: Cut it, lift it, turn it over. Three jobs, three parts, and the mouldboard is the one that changed farming.

pump.note: A chamber that changes volume and two valves that only let water go one way.

turbine.note: Blades on a shaft, and the only question is what is pushing them.

kiln.note: A box that gets hot enough and cools slowly enough, and the second half is what breaks the pot.

forge.note: Fire, air, and a way to hold what you are heating.

clock.note: A source of power, something that counts, and something that stops the counting from running away.

compass.note: A magnet free to turn, and everything else is keeping it free.

sextant.note: It measures the angle between two things, which is why it works on a moving deck when nothing else does.

barometer.note: A column of mercury the atmosphere is holding up, or a sealed box it is squeezing.

microscope.note: Two lenses in series, and a great deal of trouble getting light through the specimen.

book.note: A codex is folded sheets sewn in gatherings, which is why it opens flat and a scroll does not.

paper.note: Fibre, water, a screen to catch it on, and pressure to take the water out.

soap.note: One reaction, known for four thousand years: fat and a strong alkali.

cheese.note: Separate the curd from the whey, then decide how long you can wait.

motherboard.note: A board whose job is entirely connection: everything on it is there to let the other things talk.

operating_system.note: Everything between the metal and the program, and almost all of it is about sharing.

glass.note: The soda-lime batch that is 90% of all glass made, plus what it takes to melt and shape it.

concrete.note: Cement is the glue, aggregate is the bulk, water is the reaction; steel is what stops it failing in tension.

brick.note: Clay, water, a shape, and enough heat to make the change permanent.

rope.note: Fibre into yarn, yarn into strand, strand into rope — each layer twisted against the one below so it cannot unlay.

cloth.note: Fibre, spun, then crossed at right angles under tension.

ink.note: A colourant, something to carry it, and something to make it stay.

paint.note: Pigment carried in a binder, thinned to spread and left to harden.

mirror.note: A flat, clean sheet and a metal film behind it.

wheel.note: A rim held off its centre by spokes, and something for it to turn on.

boat.note: A shell that keeps water out, stiffened inside, with something to drive and steer it.

pot.note: Clay, a way to make it round, and fire.

coin.note: A weighed blank and two dies struck together.

leather.note: A hide stopped from rotting, then made soft again.

window.note: A hole made weathertight without being made opaque.

door.note: A panel, a way to hang it, and a way to hold it shut.

bow.note: A stave that stores energy, and a string that releases it.

drum.note: A membrane held under tension over an opening.

lock.note: Something that will not move until the right shape moves it.

barrel.note: Curved staves squeezed into a shape that holds itself together.

basket.note: Rods for the frame, weavers for the skin.

candle.note: A fuel that melts before it burns, and a wick that draws it up.

spear.note: A point, a shaft, and the joint between them — which is the part that fails.

wall.note: Something to stand on, something to stack, and something to hold the stack together.

pipe.note: A tube, a way to join tubes, and a way to stop the join leaking.

needle.note: A point, a shaft stiff enough not to bend, and an eye that does not weaken it.

knife.note: A hard edge on a tough spine, and a handle that will not come off.

hammer.note: A heavy head and a handle long enough to swing it — and an eye that keeps the two together.

magnet.note: Domains lined up, and something to stop them wandering back.

electric_motor.note: A field, a rotor in it, and a way to keep pushing the rotor the same way round.

chain.note: Links, and the weld that makes a link a link.

cannon.note: A tube strong enough to survive what happens inside it, on something that absorbs the recoil.

blade.note: A wedge, and a heat treatment that makes the wedge stay a wedge.

helmet.note: A hard shell that does not touch the head, and a liner that keeps it that way.

lever.note: A rigid bar, a fulcrum, and the choice of where to put it.

transistor.note: Two junctions in one crystal, so a small current can decide what a large one does.

rivet.note: A pin with a head, given a second head after it is through.

frame.note: Members that carry load, and joints that stop them folding.

dome.note: A shell in compression, and a way to stop it spreading at the bottom.

axle.note: A shaft that carries the wheel, and the surfaces it turns on.

chisel.note: A hardened wedge on a shaft you can hit.

roof.note: A frame that sheds water, and a skin that does not let it in.

plaster.note: A powder that sets when you wet it, on something for it to hold to.

adobe.note: Earth with enough clay to bind and enough straw to stop it cracking.

canvas.note: A plain weave heavy enough to take tension without stretching out of shape.

arrow.note: A shaft stiff enough for the bow that shoots it, weighted at the front and steered at the back.

harbour.note: Somewhere the sea stops being weather.

capacitor.note: Two plates that never touch, and something between them that will not conduct.

light_bulb.note: A wire hot enough to glow, in an atmosphere that will not let it burn.

microprocessor.note: Millions of transistors printed at once, and the wiring between them.

road.note: Layers, each one spreading the load over more of the one beneath.

beam.note: A member loaded across its length — deepest where the bending is worst.

sickle.note: A curved edge that cuts by drawing, and a handle set to keep the wrist straight.

granary.note: Dry, off the ground, and shut against everything that also eats grain.

moat.note: A ditch that either holds water or is not worth digging.

plate_armor.note: Shaped plates that overlap so the joints move and the gaps do not line up.

lyre.note: A soundbox, two arms, a crossbar, and strings you can tune.

silk.note: One continuous filament, unwound rather than spun.

felt.note: Wool, water, heat and pressure — no thread anywhere in it.

parchment.note: Skin that was never tanned — limed, stretched, and dried under tension.

arch.note: Wedges that cannot fall because there is nowhere for them to go.

crown.note: Precious metal, worked thin, made to be seen from a distance.

$not_assemblies_rule: A needs list answers 'what goes into one'. Some made things have no answer, and counting them as owing a list inflates the backlog until the sweep looks endless. A list is NOT owed for: a SHAPE or geometric feature (bevel, extrados, camber); a SURFACE or layer that is a coat of something already listed (scratch_coat, base_course); a JOINT or PROCESS (weld, tempering, honing); or a SINGLE PIECE of one material shaped by one operation (voussoir, quoin, link, shank). Each id here is a judgement somebody made and can be argued with — which is the point of writing it down rather than inferring it from tags, the way the first version of this denominator did.
